## Pull request overview

This PR adds a substantially expanded documentation set intended to bridge the gap between basic component reference and real-world/production usage, including new getting-started guides, advanced patterns, and a new “Case Studies” section.

**Changes:**
- Adds new Guide docs: quick start, installation, zero-to-deployment tutorial, video tutorial curriculum, and advanced guides (custom components, plugin development, performance, security).
- Introduces a new `/docs/case-studies` section with an index, taxonomy (`meta.json`), and multiple long-form case studies.
- Updates docs navigation metadata to surface the new guide pages and case studies section.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 16 out of 16 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments.

<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |

This documentation example executes arbitrary JavaScript via `new Function(...)` for `transform`. That is code-injection prone and unsafe to recommend in a plugin guide. Prefer using the project’s expression/evaluator utilities (or a sandboxed expression language) and clearly document what expression syntax is allowed.

The CSP example explicitly allows `script-src 'unsafe-inline'`, which significantly weakens CSP protections and is generally discouraged in a “Security Best Practices” guide. Consider demonstrating a nonce/hash-based CSP (and removing `unsafe-inline` for scripts), while optionally noting tradeoffs and when inline scripts/styles might be unavoidable.

The Bilibili section includes non-English text (e.g., Chinese link text and feature bullets). This repo’s docs should keep all user-facing documentation text in English; consider translating these lines to English and (if needed) linking to a separate localized page for Chinese content.

This example uses an inline `style={{ ... }}` prop, which conflicts with the project’s Tailwind-first approach and makes patterns harder to copy/paste consistently. Prefer a Tailwind utility/arbitrary property class (or a documented Tailwind plugin extension) instead of inline styles.

The example memoizes `SchemaRenderer` by comparing `JSON.stringify(prevProps.schema)` to `JSON.stringify(nextProps.schema)`. This is O(n) every render and can be slower than re-rendering; it also breaks if the schema contains non-serializable values. Prefer ensuring the schema object reference is stable (e.g., `useMemo`) or using a targeted comparison of the specific fields that matter.
```suggestion
const MemoizedSchemaRenderer = memo(SchemaRenderer);
```
